Cylindrical drums are usually two-headed with straight sides, and sometimes carry a buzzing striking string. The Iranian dohol is the famous form of the cylindrical drum. Many musical regions of the Middle East, North Africa and Central Asia have the dohol and variants of the cylindrical drum, including the Armenian dhol, the Kurdish dawal and the Egyptian tabl.
圓柱鼓的鼓身通常採用胡桃木、楸木或其他硬質木材製成，具有良好的共鳴特性。鼓面與鼓: The body of a cylindrical drum is usually walnut, alder or another hardwood with good resonating qualities. Both heads are goatskin or cowhide, treated so as to give the best sound. The rims are mostly reinforced with wood or metal. The buzzing string is of natural fibre or metal wire, fitted inside the drum to produce its particular buzzing colour. Making varies a little from region to region, but the basic materials are similar.
圓柱鼓起源於中東、北非及中亞地區，是人類打擊樂器發展中的重要形式。其歷史可追溯至: The cylindrical drum originated in the Middle East, North Africa and Central Asia and is an important form in the development of percussion. Its history can be traced to the ancient civilisations, and local peoples used drums of this kind widely in religious ritual, war and social entertainment. The Iranian dohol is the most representative development of the cylindrical drum, with its own timbre and technique. With the expansion of Islamic culture and the trade of the Silk Road the cylindrical drum spread gradually to the surrounding regions. Regional variants arose in response, the Armenian dhol, the Kurdish dawal and the Egyptian tabl, each improved according to local tradition. These instruments kept the basic two-headed cylindrical structure and also took on local musical styles, becoming an important part of the folk music of the Middle East and North Africa, and they continue today.
圓柱鼓音色渾厚而富有穿透力，具有溫暖的中低音質感。其雙面設計賦予樂器多層次的共鳴: The cylindrical drum has a thick, carrying timbre with a warm low and middle quality. Its two-headed design gives it a layered resonance, and the two heads produce different colours: the top head is brighter and clearer, the bottom deeper and darker. The range lies mainly in the low and middle frequencies, with strong penetration and projection. When a striking string is used it adds a buzzing quality on top of the basic drum sound, adding a further layer. Compared with the exact pitch of a timpani the cylindrical drum is more veiled and more rhythmic; compared with the Brazilian bongo its tone is deeper and more forceful. Drums of this kind create the distinctive warm, bleak national colour of Middle Eastern and Central Asian music.
